cim: Ohio lawyer suspended after citing fake AI-generated cases
cim_eredeti: Ohio lawyer suspended after citing fake AI-generated cases
szoveg_eredeti:
The Ohio Supreme Court on Nov. 24 indefinitely suspended the law license of an attorney who cited four artificial intelligence-hallucinated cases that didn't exist, made false statements to courts and violated other ethics rules.

Attorney Arleesha Wilson owes more than $647,000 in judgments for neglecting client matters, providing incompetent representation, and making false statements to courts.

In April 2025, Wilson filed a brief in federal court in a case against the city of Cleveland. The city's legal team raised a red flag: four of the cases she cited didn't exist. The court told Wilson to provide copies of the cases by September.

Wilson turned in 1,395 pages of case law. But the four cases were not among them, the court found.

At a contempt hearing, Wilson admitted using artificial intelligence to draft the brief. The court ordered her to pay a $7,500 penalty by the end of November 2025. She did not, according to the disciplinary case.

Artificial intelligence tools can produce false or misleading information and fabricated cases, according to the National Center for State Courts. "Never trust, always verify. Check every citation, case, statute, rule, and claim," the center tells attorneys using AI tools.

It wasn't just the AI cases that got Wilson into trouble. In 2025, the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association filed a disciplinary case against Wilson, alleging that she failed clients in a roofing contract dispute. The clients won a $625,000 judgment against Wilson for legal malpractice, and she was ordered to pay more than $14,000 to the roofing company's attorney.

Wilson, who was admitted to the bar in 2018, earned her law degree from Cleveland State University.

State government reporter Laura Bischoff can be reached at lbischoff@usatodayco.com and @lbischoff on X.
